lines.text: Every stone in the farm was ringing. Somewhere far above us, a door crashed open. Then another. Then boots, a great many of them, coming down.
They came down the stairs in dark red armour, with iron dog-jaws over their faces and crossbows already raised. The Hounds.
And behind them, taking the steps two at a time, came the only man in Aldcrown with six rings and no mask.
Every door in this cathedral was watched, little lord. Nobody thought to watch the drains. I'll have someone flogged for that. After.
Then the bolts came.
Wren shot back from behind an alcove, three arrows for every bolt. Tamsin ran with Nell in her arms. Ilse ran beside her, holding Oswin's cloak over the child like a shield.
Oswin turned to hold the Hounds back. He had one good arm, a borrowed sword, and burns from neck to waist. He held them anyway. For a while.
Then Caddoc's fire found him. I felt it hit, a burning cold that went straight through my own ribs.
I'm fine! Keep running!
You're on fire again!
Slightly!
We dragged him with us. There was only one way left to go. The way up was full of Hounds. So we went down.
The stair down was narrow, cut deep into the rock. Wide enough for one man at a time. Or one very large dog.
Ash stopped at the top of it, and turned around.
Ash! Ash, come!
He didn't come. He stood in the mouth of the stair with his ears flat and his lips drawn back, and the Hounds coming at him. He had never once sat when he was told.
I felt every blow he took. A bolt in the shoulder. A net that tore. Fire across his back. And every time, the Hounds fell back a step.
Shoot the dog! Shoot it! It's only a dog!
It wasn't only a dog. It took them a long time to work that out.
When Ash finally came down the stair after us, smoking and bleeding and wagging his tail, the Hounds above had stopped coming. For now.
We hid in a dead-end chamber at the bottom, with Oswin bleeding into my cloak and Nell asleep against Ash's side. And then a thread pulled tight inside me, so sharp I cried out.
Not one of ours down here. One far away, across the city. Hobb's. And Hobb was frightened.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and three, coming soon.
